title: REMEMBERING SO WE DO NOT FORGET

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: We completely destroyed them, as we had done with Sihon king of Heshbon, destroying every city—men, women and children. But all the livestock and the plunder from their cities we carried off for ourselves. So at that time we took from these two kings of the Amorites the territory east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Gorge as far as Mount Hermon. (Hermon is called Sirion by the Sidonians; the Amorites call it Senir.) - Deut 3:6-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses recounts the sober reality of the conquest and then carefully records the extent of the territory taken — from the Arnon Gorge to Mount Hermon. He even notes the different names the surrounding peoples used for Hermon. Why such detail? Because Moses was helping the new generation remember exactly what God had done. These were real places, real victories, real evidence of God's faithfulness. Recording them preserved the memory for generations to come.

We must again handle the hard reality of this passage honestly, keeping it in its redemptive-historical setting as an act of divine judgment on the Amorites at a unique moment, not a model for how God's people act today. Held in that context, Moses' careful record teaches us something valuable about remembering God's works.

God's people are prone to forget. When the memory of God's faithfulness fades, faith grows weak and fear creeps back in. So throughout Scripture, God's people are urged to remember, to record, to rehearse what God has done. Moses was building a memorial in words, ensuring the next generation would know how God had provided.

This is a wise practice for us too. When we take time to remember and record God's faithfulness in our lives — the answered prayers, the provisions, the deliverances — we strengthen our faith for the future. Forgetting breeds fear and doubt; remembering breeds gratitude and trust. The greatest thing we remember is what God has done in Christ, which is why Jesus gave us the Lord's Supper as a memorial: "Do this in remembrance of me" (Luke 22:19). Keep a record of God's faithfulness, and let remembering fuel your trust.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take time to remember and record God's faithfulness in your life?
2. How does forgetting God's works weaken faith, and remembering strengthen it?
3. How does the Lord's Supper help you remember what God has done in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me not to forget Your faithfulness. Teach me to remember and record what You have done, so that my faith is strengthened and my heart stays grateful, especially as I remember the work of Christ. Amen.
